There's a clear difference in experience
between an MFG driver in his first race,
and one in his third.

Sena's biggest strength is
how monstrously quickly he learns.

He has a prodigious talent for absorbing
what he experiences and using it himself.

Did you tell Sena about the weakness in
Katagiri Kanata's style the boss told us about?

Hell no. If he can't figure it while he's out
there racing him, there's no point doing this.
This is humiliating.

He overwhelmed me emotionally,
and I couldn't do a damn thing.

When it comes to Gunma pride,
Katagiri Kanata outdid me.
Katagiri Kanata is ahead now?

In all honesty, he strikes me
as the bigger problem.
KATAGIRI KANATA

And now that she's available,
let's chat with Marie-chan—

I-Is there some reason you look so eager
to be asked about this?

I feel like your plans for summer
won't amount to much, but I'll ask anyway.

So mean. Aren't you being
a little harsh, Uehara-san?
My plans for summer...
involve a strategy for losing weight!

Whether I like it or not,
I'll go to the gym and sweat a bunch

until my body is perfect
for a cute swimsuit,
and then, I'll seduce you, Uehara-san.
I see.

I won't get my hopes up,
but I wish you luck.
Now, head back to your position, yeah?
You're so mean, Uehara-san!

How are you going to
get past that Porsche?

I couldn't pull it off,
no matter what I tried,
but I get the feeling you can.

Show me what you've got,
so I can learn from it.

Take me into a zone
I've never seen before.
MF GHOST
INTO THE FINAL LAP
The trio negotiate City Hall corner.

They're almost done with
the peninsula section for a fourth lap.

The 885 car has fallen back a place
after a failed overtake on the 1 car,

and almost as if taking up the baton
from his fellow rookie,

the 86 is now in position
to strike and pass the 1!
Don't look away, folks.

Since a fire was lit under Katagiri
Kanata, he's shot through the field
with the precision of a sniper.

Will the former champ manage to prevent
the red bullet from hitting its mark?

Katagiri Kanata has this uncanny knack
that must frighten other drivers.

Ishigami-kun's probably in a cold sweat,
even if he'd never admit it.

They blast past the post office
at full throttle.

And once again, the scent
of danger is in the air!
This is it. He's gonna try something.

The 86 is pulsing with
aggression right now.

And there he goes!
The 86 makes its move!
And he's through!
The 86 pulls ahead of the 1 car!

Another split-second kill!
Even Ishigami Fujin couldn't stop him!

What in the world did we
just see, Akiyama-san?
A surprise, for sure.

I never even considered
that kind of maneuver.

He took advantage of an inherent
weakness in European supercars.

There's a pronounced height difference
in the roads on that second hairpin,

meaning a car with lower ground
clearance can't take the shortest line.

The 86 isn't that much higher off the
ground, but relative to the 911 GT3,
it had enough to daringly cut inside.

The chassis struck the road.
Will that be a problem?
I even saw sparks.
Holy cow.
I don't think it'll be a problem.
Kanata's playing rough today.
And onto the back straightaway!

This is the stretch with
the second-highest recorded speeds.

Can the 1 car with its superior
horsepower come back at him?

This stretch until the Nushiya corner
allows them to open the throttle,

but due to the undulating nature of
the road, there's only one ideal line.
I'm very impressed with Katagiri Kanata.

He's positioning his car perfectly
to stop the 1 from getting past.

I think we can now be sure that the 86
has received a substantial upgrade
under the hood for this third race.

Otherwise, no matter
how perfect his line was,

he wouldn't be able to fend off
the 1 car on this back straight.
They enter the Nushiya corner.

He first pulls the kinda tricks
you only see in street racing,

and now he's showing the experience
of a seasoned racing driver.

Nice. The stronger the enemy,
the more satisfying it is to beat 'em.
Now I'm really fired up!
Getting old is no fun at all.
Incredible.

He's displaying a different kind
of prowess from the first two races.

Something must've awakened
inside Katagiri Kanata.

Was this otherworldy sprinting prowess
nurtured by that genius downhill racer?

Our lead group finishes up its fourth lap
and heads into the final lap.

Michael Beckenbauer.
Sawatari Koki. And Akaba Kaito.

With the 2 leading the way,
it's a three-way brawl for first.

And six seconds back is the 86,
fresh from its latest skirmish!

He's all the way back up to fourth,
and is showing no signs of slowing down.

The super rookie is really
earning that title today!
Katagiri Kanata's awesome!
Knock Beckenbauer off his perch!

Ishigami in the 1 car is in fifth,
with Moroboshi's 885 in sixth.

Oishi in the 3 is seventh.
Yanagida in the 6 is eighth.

Maezono's 13 car is in ninth.
Sakamoto's 14 is in tenth.
Aiba in the 9 runs 11th.

Yashio's 12 is in 12th.
Kitahara in the 18 car is 13th.
Taylor in the 8 is 14th.
And Otani's 7 car in 15th.

These 15 sprinters
will now go flat-out...
to gain as much ground as they can.

I'd like to ask about something
that's been on my mind, Akiyama-san.
Shoot.

Is there a reason the lights in the
three tunnels have been turned off?
This might be a good chance to explain.

MFG as a racing series
was originally started

with the intention of reviving areas
affected by the eruption of Mount Fuji.

I'm sure fans are aware that
a significant portion of the proceeds

is donated to the areas
that were hardest hit.

The natural disaster resulted
in a protracted period

where infrastructure shut down, leaving
residents without electricity for a time.

Shutting off the lights in the tunnel
is a reminder of those events
by MFG's organizers.
It's also for this very same reason

that all five MFG courses include
hazards that reflect the Fuji eruption.

I can see why the organizing committee
chose you as a spokesman, Akiyama-san.

You have a wealth of fascinating
insights into their vision.

And now, back to the race.
Into the Black and White they go!

He's left the most enticing line open.
I'm not sure what he's planning,

but if there's space to overtake,
my policy is to go for it.

Go on, horsepower honcho.
Give him a taste of your top speed.
The 2 moves out from the 12's slipstream.
And the 4's right behind him!

You were aiming for
that pocket of air all along?
Well played, Sawatari.
How d'ya like me now?

You enjoying your taste
of that monstrous 670 horsepower?

The Midnight Straight on this final lap
is turning into an test of strength.

The acoustics of the tunnel
enhance the music of the Ferrari.
And he passes both cars!

First down to third
have all switched places!
There's the lead group.
Will I be able to catch them?
Fujiwara-sensei always told me:

"When you want to achieve something,
don't frame it like a question."
"Make it a statement in the future tense."
I can do this. I will catch them.
MF Ghost.
And through he goes!
The 885 finally blasts past the 1 car!
He passed him around the outside.

I believe he imitated Katagiri Kanata
in the line he took.
Despite only seeing it two or three times,

he seems on the verge of
getting that ability down pat.

It's a real surprise. He's proving
to be a fearsome rookie.

He's a different type of driver
than Katagiri Kanata,

but I sense huge potential for growth,
albeit on a path that's hard to predict.
Aiba Shun. So you've made it this far up.

But I'll stop you in your tracks
if it's the last thing I do!

Here we have two drivers
who seem to butt heads regularly.

Both are heavyweights
with comparable power.

Is this going to be another clash
between the pair?
And back to the lead group!

The 2 car's superior power
is on full display.
The two cars behind can't catch him.
I can't keep up. What's this guy's deal?

The 2 car charges onward,
with the 4 and the 15 giving chase.
Akaba-kun's taken the lead,

and I reckon the peninsula section
is where he'll win or lose it.

His previous best there is nowhere near
Beckenbauer's or Sawatari-kun's.

So if Akaba-kun is still in the lead
at the end of that section,

I'd say he has one hand
on the winner's trophy.

The two cars behind
won't make it easy, though.

Those two have proven they're the
cream of the crop in this season of MFG.
And there they go.

Next up, the peninsula section, and the
course is named after it for good reason.

But we can't forget about this car
that's chasing them down!

The holder of the record
for this section: Katagiri Kanata.

The fastest man on the peninsula
is coming their way!

Katagiri-kun is particularly fast
in this stretch.

You could even say, given his
previous trouble in this area,

Akaba-kun being in the lead presents
an opportunity for Katagiri-kun.
How much ground can he gain on them?

You'll wanna keep your eyes
glued to this race, folks!

This is bad. I'm so tense,
my stomach's killing me.
I'm gonna puke.
Please don't. Not in here.

At this point, there's not a whole lot
we can do from this end.

Feel free to go to the bathroom
to take care of business.
I can't.
I can't leave the booth. Not now.

We're on the final lap, and my partner's
out there on a miracle run.
They're closing up!

The gaps between
the top three are shrinking!

But these peninsula roads are narrow,
and overtaking will be a tall order.

Akaba Kaito is spurred on by his pride
as last year's second-placed driver.

The prancing horse is
determined to get away!
What's wrong? Shake a leg, Sawatari.

Passing the 2 should
be child's play for us.
I'm letting you make the first move.
All three cars are bumper to bumper,

and it's hard to ignore the feeling
that something's about to happen.

The one advantage this car has
over the Ferrari is that it's lighter.

If I wanna make the most
of that advantage...

a downhill battle on the brakes
seems the best way!
I've never liked guys like you,

who chase any girls
that cross their path.
Where's the beauty in that?

My Seventeen Complex,
on the other hand...
is the embodiment of my aesthetic!
And the 4 car takes the lead!
Sawatari Koki is now in first place!

If you ask me, a womanizer with
no standards could never be as cool...
as a fetish enthusiast.
Sawatari Koki is a beast!

His overflowing fighting spirit
led to a fearsome overtake.

Now try to hold that snotty German back
for as long as you can, Akaba-san.
That way, I can build up a decent margin.

And wait, is that the 12
making its move?

The 2 crosses behind the 12
in an attempt to go on the attack.

He's relying on horsepower alone
to pass him around the outside.

But he fails! The first fork on the
course ends up blocking his path!
Akaba Kaito drops to third!
Damn it.
Aw, crap. Michael's already on my tail.

Unbelievable. What are you
doing back there, Akaba-san?

This is every bit as
shocking as it is brutal!
Akaba Kaito has been crushed.
Out of respect for Akaba-kun...

I'll point out that he made no mistakes
and there were no issues with his driving.

It's just the two drivers he's up against
are driving at a truly absurd level.
They're fundamentally built different.

That was evident when they both
set course records in qualifying.

This is really turning
into a wild season.

The new generation is improving too fast
for the vets and journeymen to keep up.
They've been left behind.

Those maniacs. They don't even hesitate
at the thought of trading paint,

nor think twice about the kind of
roughhousing that can get them flagged.

I'll never forget how
frustrating this feels.
Katagiri Kanata? Where'd he spring from?
The Mitsuishi corner!
Here he goes!

The 86 is making a move
down the inside!
They're side-by-side! It's getting tight!
And he's through!
An overtake!
Katagiri Kanata reclaims third place!
That was razor-sharp.

And a reminder that all three of
these drivers set new course records!

And lest we forget, Katagiri Kanata set
the record for this peninsula section!

He's driving like he wants
to remind us of that fact!

I exited on a slightly wider
line than I visualized.
I'm starting to understeer.
What an incredible race.
The Odawara studio is buzzing.

Our leaders are now zooming
through the coastal area.

Look at the distances!
The 86 has really dug in deep!

There's no telling what the outcome
of this race might be at this point.

And this tricolor group of cars
continue to duke it out!

On any other day, Aiba's tires would be

So why the hell isn't the same true today?

If anything, it's my front
that's starting to feel jumpy.

Can't believe my mid-engine 4x4 handicap
has come to bite me so late in the game.

The two cars fighting over ninth
are approaching the third fork!

We've seen such drama

and now, it looks like Aiba in the 9

But can he pull it off?
Whoa!

He didn't go for it.
Not even an attempt.

Don't go getting your hopes up.
I'm not a technical racer.

It's the 86!

The king, Beckenbauer, has just

That pass was so smooth...
...it was like magic!

I'm having trouble believing
what I just saw.
What the heck was that, Akiyama-san?
The gutter.

He used the height difference
between the asphalt and the shoulder.
But boy, that really takes me back.

That was actually one of
Fujiwara Takumi's favorite tricks.

I have to say, this kid
never runs out of surprises.
Is it because of his tires?

He never tried anything like that

are his tires starting
